alan: Proposal — region-aware spot fallback priority to cut egress and improve availability.

alan: TL;DR: prefer local warm pools -> same-region alt instance types -> cross-region as last resort. Add a node taint `spot-fallback=reserved:NoSchedule` during handoff and use a lifecycle hook to annotate nodes on termination.

marta: Nice. How do we make the cluster-autoscaler prefer warm spares? CA supports multiple node groups but we need a priority hint.

jin: We can use node affinity + taints. Also consider PDBs for stateful workloads. Local PVs are the tricky bit.

infra-bot: CI check: autoscaler helm chart changes detected. Need CA >= v1.31 for prioritized nodePools. Canary slated for prod-cluster-a.

sam: Draft lifecycle hook (on termination):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
NODE="$NODE_NAME"
kubectl annotate node "$NODE" infra.redwood/spot-fallback-at=$(date -u +%s)
kubectl taint node "$NODE" spot-fallback=reserved:NoSchedule --overwrite
# trigger graceful eviction via eviction API
kubectl patch pod -n kube-system my-evictor --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"evict":"'$NODE'"}}}}}'
```

sam: And simple quick commands:
```
kubectl taint nodes <node> spot-fallback=reserved:NoSchedule
kubectl annotate node <node> infra.redwood/spot-fallbacking=true
```

leah: Cost note: cross-region fallback increases egress and latency. Sometimes cheaper spot prices in other region still win — we need a floor that includes egress+network transit. I'll add to the sim.

ops-oncall: If we cross regions, verify KMS and service account access + DNS routing. Also inform SRE oncall for the canary window.

marta: I'll run a 7-day Monte Carlo sim using historical interruption rates + our egress matrix. Will post results by Fri.

alan: Plan: marta runs sim, jin wires CA+taint rules, sam finalizes lifecycle hook. Canary in prod-cluster-a next Mon. @ops-oncall please stand by. :thumbsup:
